summary: The code provides two utility functions for filtering customer lists: one to find customers who have placed orders, and another to extract unique email addresses. Overall the code is clean and readable, though it uses O(N*M) and O(K^2) approaches respectively which could impact performance on larger datasets.

issues.description: Nested loops result in O(N * M) time complexity, which can be inefficient for large lists of customers and orders.
issues.suggestion: Build a set of order customer IDs beforehand for O(N + M) lookup: order_customer_ids = {order["customer_id"] for order in orders} and return [c for c in customers if c["id"] in order_customer_ids]

issues.description: Checking membership in a list takes O(K) time per iteration, leading to O(K^2) overall complexity.
issues.suggestion: Use a set to track seen emails: seen = set(); return [c["email"] for c in customers if c["email"] not in seen and not seen.add(c["email"])]

suggestions: Consider adding type hints for return structures if more detailed models are used.
Add unit tests covering edge cases such as empty lists or missing keys.
